Returns the most recent computed summary immediately (even if a little stale), or a cheap "still gathering" placeholder if none has been computed yet, and kicks off a background recompute when the cache is stale. It never runs the full-table SQLite scans on the caller's thread, so it can't stall Netty request or workspace-search dispatcher threads — the cold first computeSummary() (which can take many seconds on a large database) no longer blocks the welcome response or, by dispatcher starvation, a document the user clicks right after. |

### CoroutineProfiles { #coroutineprofiling-kt-coroutineprofiles }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">object</span> <span class="nc">CoroutineProfiles</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/app/diagnostics/CoroutineProfiling/#L72)

Box-owned continuation instrumentation, shared by Runloop and SimulationClock. A continuation's CPU/heap counters exclude its suspended lifetime. No timers or allocations on the disabled dispatch path. Export copies happen on request, not per resume. A process permits one capture at a time; document isolation also applies to stop/snapshot.

### FrameProfile { #frameprofile-kt-frameprofile }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">FrameProfile</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">private</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">context</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">CoroutineContext</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">name</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="s">&quot;Frame&quot;</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">targetFps</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">60.0</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">allocationKiB</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">512.0</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">AutoCloseable</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/app/diagnostics/FrameProfile/#L61)

Explicit frame boundaries for the existing Profiling panel. This object does not start a capture. Press Record in the panel, then call `beginFrame` once per application frame, on a stable thread. Intervals include time between boxes and waits; CPU/heap counters cover that thread only. Use `measure` for named inclusive stages. No counter reads or sample allocation while recording is off.

## PinnedConsole.kt { #pinnedconsole-kt }

A `LogSink` that pins chosen channels to a small, non-scrolling region at the *top* of the
terminal while every other log line scrolls normally below it.

The heavy lifting is a single ANSI scroll-region (DECSTBM): the top N rows are fenced off so
ordinary output can only scroll in the region beneath them, which means a plain `println` "just
works" — there is no per-frame render loop over application state. The header is repainted only
when a pinned value actually changes (coalesced by a single daemon tick), and the terminal size
is re-checked about once a second.

Selection is by channel tag: a log event whose comma-separated `channel` contains a pinned tag
(e.g. pinning `"audio"` matches `"info,audio"`) updates that tag's row instead of scrolling.
Configure via the `AFIELD_PIN_CHANNELS` env var (comma/space separated) and/or at runtime with
`pin`/`unpin`/`clear`.

Degrades cleanly: if stdout is not an interactive TTY, ANSI/cursor control is unavailable, or the
terminal is a legacy Windows console (Mordant reports `AnsiLevel.NONE`), pinning switches off and
every event — pinned or not — simply scrolls, with would-be-pinned lines tagged `pin` so they
stay visible. Set `AFIELD_PIN_DISABLE=1` to force this fallback.

Known limitation: raw `System.out.println`/stderr writes elsewhere in the app bypass this sink's
lock and can, very occasionally, interleave with a header repaint. They still scroll below the
header; the visual glitch is transient. Routing all app output through the dispatcher avoids it.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/app/diagnostics/logging/PinnedConsole.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/app/diagnostics/logging/PinnedConsole/)

### PinnedChannel { #pinnedconsole-kt-pinnedchannel }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">PinnedChannel</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">tag</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">heatmap</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="kc">true</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/app/diagnostics/logging/PinnedConsole/#L50)

A channel to pin, at "channel picking" time (see `PinnedConsole.install`/`PinnedConsole.pin`). `heatmap` colors the channel's rolling numeric values (`foo=1.2ms`) blue-through-red by whether they fell or rose since the channel's last line; it's on by default and opt-out per channel.

Cheap enough to call every frame: the row shows an animated spinner + beats/sec while beats keep arriving, and freezes to "idle" when they stop. No-op if the console isn't installed or isn't rendering (non-TTY). Use this instead of a per-frame `lprintln`/`print`. |
| [<code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">error</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">key</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">title</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">lines</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">List</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">&gt;</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/app/diagnostics/logging/PinnedConsole/#L174) | Pin a compilation/execution error as a sticky, multi-line panel at the very *top* of the header, keyed by `key` (use a stable id such as the box id so re-runs replace the same panel). Unlike the channel rows, an error panel never expires on the silence timer — a broken build stays put until `clearError` is called (typically on the next clean compile) or a fresh `error` for the same `key` replaces it. `title` is a short one-line summary; `lines` are the detail (each clipped to width, the panel body capped in height with a "+N more" tail). No-op when pinning is off (non-TTY); the error still scrolls via whatever `error`-channel line the caller already logged. |

## stdlib_diagnostics.kt { #stdlib-diagnostics-kt }

The general-purpose helpers that every Field box already has in scope.

Box code is compiled with the standard imports in `intro` in its preamble and with `Box` as an
implicit receiver, so everything here — including the `Box.` extensions — can be called
unqualified from inside a box.

The substantial part is the property-delegate machinery that `prop` and `@exported` generate
against: [`Delegation`](workspace.md#stdlib-properties-kt-delegation) (stores on the receiver's own property bag), [`Inheritance`](workspace.md#stdlib-properties-kt-inheritance) (walks up
`parents` until some ancestor has the property, otherwise throws
[`MissingInheritedPropertyException`](workspace.md#stdlib-properties-kt-missinginheritedpropertyexception) with a message naming the property and the box), and
[`InheritanceFromContext`](workspace.md#stdlib-properties-kt-inheritancefromcontext) (same walk, but prefers each box's live Kotlin variables over raw
properties).

The rest is small conveniences: graph access (`named`, `+=` / `-=` for
connect/disconnect, `__m` markers); execution control (`begin`, `end`, `start`, `animate`,
`aside`, `cell`); frame-presentation logging (`frameLogStart`, `frameLogStop`,
`frameLogMark`, `frameLogLine`); matrix and buffer building (`mat4`, `mat3`, `FloatBuffer.add`,
`IntBuffer.add`, `ByteBuffer.putf16`); and terse numeric/collection/string shorthands
(`Number.f` / `.i` / `.l` / `.d`, `fa`, `ia`, `Int.alphas`, `String.times`, `List.m` / `.s`,
`String.r`, and `highlightSyntax` behind `String.h` / `String.ss`).

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/app/diagnostics/stdlib_diagnostics.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/app/diagnostics/stdlib_diagnostics/)

unqualified from inside a box.

The substantial part is the property-delegate machinery that `prop` and `@exported` generate
against: [`Delegation`](workspace.md#stdlib-properties-kt-delegation) (stores on the receiver's own property bag), [`Inheritance`](workspace.md#stdlib-properties-kt-inheritance) (walks up
`parents` until some ancestor has the property, otherwise throws
[`MissingInheritedPropertyException`](workspace.md#stdlib-properties-kt-missinginheritedpropertyexception) with a message naming the property and the box), and
[`InheritanceFromContext`](workspace.md#stdlib-properties-kt-inheritancefromcontext) (same walk, but prefers each box's live Kotlin variables over raw
properties).

The rest is small conveniences: graph access (`named`, `+=` / `-=` for
connect/disconnect, `__m` markers); execution control (`begin`, `end`, `start`, `animate`,
`aside`, `cell`); frame-presentation logging (`frameLogStart`, `frameLogStop`,
`frameLogMark`, `frameLogLine`); matrix and buffer building (`mat4`, `mat3`, `FloatBuffer.add`,
`IntBuffer.add`, `ByteBuffer.putf16`); and terse numeric/collection/string shorthands
(`Number.f` / `.i` / `.l` / `.d`, `fa`, `ia`, `Int.alphas`, `String.times`, `List.m` / `.s`,
`String.r`, and `highlightSyntax` behind `String.h` / `String.ss`).

## stdlib_graph.kt { #stdlib-graph-kt }

The general-purpose helpers that every Field box already has in scope.

Box code is compiled with the standard imports in `intro` in its preamble and with `Box` as an
implicit receiver, so everything here — including the `Box.` extensions — can be called
unqualified from inside a box.

The substantial part is the property-delegate machinery that `prop` and `@exported` generate
against: [`Delegation`](workspace.md#stdlib-properties-kt-delegation) (stores on the receiver's own property bag), [`Inheritance`](workspace.md#stdlib-properties-kt-inheritance) (walks up
`parents` until some ancestor has the property, otherwise throws
[`MissingInheritedPropertyException`](workspace.md#stdlib-properties-kt-missinginheritedpropertyexception) with a message naming the property and the box), and
[`InheritanceFromContext`](workspace.md#stdlib-properties-kt-inheritancefromcontext) (same walk, but prefers each box's live Kotlin variables over raw
properties).

The rest is small conveniences: graph access (`named`, `+=` / `-=` for
connect/disconnect, `__m` markers); execution control (`begin`, `end`, `start`, `animate`,
`aside`, `cell`); frame-presentation logging (`frameLogStart`, `frameLogStop`,
`frameLogMark`, `frameLogLine`); matrix and buffer building (`mat4`, `mat3`, `FloatBuffer.add`,
`IntBuffer.add`, `ByteBuffer.putf16`); and terse numeric/collection/string shorthands
(`Number.f` / `.i` / `.l` / `.d`, `fa`, `ia`, `Int.alphas`, `String.times`, `List.m` / `.s`,
`String.r`, and `highlightSyntax` behind `String.h` / `String.ss`).

## props.kt { #props-kt }

The `prop` / `rootProp` macro pair — the typed, inheritable box-property slot.

`prop` and `rootProp` exist only as the declarations that make `prop<Int>(foo)` resolve; neither
is meant to run, and calling one throws `MacroRegistry.MacroNotExpandedException`. The real work
happens at expansion time in `macro_prop` and `macro_root_prop`, which are handed the type
argument and the name, and return an `Insert` that rewrites the call site to the bare name (or
`root.name`) and pushes two declarations into the box's preamble: a
`var Box.<name> by Inheritance<T>()`, a `val Once.<name> by Onceing<T>()` and a
`val Why.<name> by Whying()` (so `why.<name>` explains where the value comes from). All three generated
lines carry the trailing empty-comment marker that makes the preamble gather copy them down into
child boxes, and an import for `T` is added via `kotlinImportStatementFor`. `macro_root_prop`
differs only in targeting `this.root`, so the accessors land on the document root rather than
on the calling box.

## reactiveProps.kt { #reactiveprops-kt }

`propUp`, `propDown` and `propUpDown`: `prop` with re-execution attached.

All three declare the same typed, inherited slot `prop` does (a `var Box.<name>` in the preamble,
copied down into children), and read and write it the same way. What they add:

- **Up** — a read that finds no value anywhere up the graph runs the box that supplies it, then
  reads again. The supplier is the box that declared the property (or supplied it before), nearest
  first, and the run happens *inside* the read, so a chain of them unwinds in order.
- **Down** — a write that changes the value reruns, after the writing box's run has finished,
  every box that read the old value, in dependency order.

Declare it where the value is written (Down is decided by the writer's declaration, Up by the
reader's), and the declaration reaches the children as `prop`'s does. The scheduling is
`afield.runtime.lifecycle.ReactiveRuns`; what it did is in `ReactiveRuns.recentEvents()`.

## stdlib_properties.kt { #stdlib-properties-kt }

The general-purpose helpers that every Field box already has in scope.

Box code is compiled with the standard imports in `intro` in its preamble and with `Box` as an
implicit receiver, so everything here — including the `Box.` extensions — can be called
unqualified from inside a box.

The substantial part is the property-delegate machinery that `prop` and `@exported` generate
against: [`Delegation`](workspace.md#stdlib-properties-kt-delegation) (stores on the receiver's own property bag), [`Inheritance`](workspace.md#stdlib-properties-kt-inheritance) (walks up
`parents` until some ancestor has the property, otherwise throws
[`MissingInheritedPropertyException`](workspace.md#stdlib-properties-kt-missinginheritedpropertyexception) with a message naming the property and the box), and
[`InheritanceFromContext`](workspace.md#stdlib-properties-kt-inheritancefromcontext) (same walk, but prefers each box's live Kotlin variables over raw
properties).

The rest is small conveniences: graph access (`named`, `+=` / `-=` for
connect/disconnect, `__m` markers); execution control (`begin`, `end`, `start`, `animate`,
`aside`, `cell`); frame-presentation logging (`frameLogStart`, `frameLogStop`,
`frameLogMark`, `frameLogLine`); matrix and buffer building (`mat4`, `mat3`, `FloatBuffer.add`,
`IntBuffer.add`, `ByteBuffer.putf16`); and terse numeric/collection/string shorthands
(`Number.f` / `.i` / `.l` / `.d`, `fa`, `ia`, `Int.alphas`, `String.times`, `List.m` / `.s`,
`String.r`, and `highlightSyntax` behind `String.h` / `String.ss`).

### Kits { #kits-kt-kits }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">object</span> <span class="nc">Kits</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/document/workspace/Kits/#L83)

Kits: one machine, many documents. A kit is what every document of one kind receives: the code of the boxes that play its roles (providers), the sources those boxes hold in other properties (a rule set, a recipe), and the asset files they read from the document's `files/` folder. It is a directory with a `kit.json` beside those files; `tools/field_kit.py` makes one from a document, rehashes it, installs it in a document, migrates a document to a newer revision and publishes it as a Welcome starting point. `public/docs/kits.md` is the user's page.

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">WelcomeDirCandidate</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">filename</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">dir</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">File</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">metadataFile</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">File</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">lastModifiedEpochMs</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Long</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">sizeBytes</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Long</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/document/workspace/dir/#L755)

A workspace document discovered by `welcomeDirCandidates`, described only by cheap `stat` metadata. Turning one into a [`WelcomeEntry`](workspace.md#dir-kt-welcomeentry) (box count + tags) requires parsing its metadata file, which `summarizeWelcomeCandidate` does lazily.

## stdlib_buffers.kt { #stdlib-buffers-kt }

The general-purpose helpers that every Field box already has in scope.

Box code is compiled with the standard imports in `intro` in its preamble and with `Box` as an
implicit receiver, so everything here — including the `Box.` extensions — can be called
unqualified from inside a box.

The substantial part is the property-delegate machinery that `prop` and `@exported` generate
against: [`Delegation`](workspace.md#stdlib-properties-kt-delegation) (stores on the receiver's own property bag), [`Inheritance`](workspace.md#stdlib-properties-kt-inheritance) (walks up
`parents` until some ancestor has the property, otherwise throws
[`MissingInheritedPropertyException`](workspace.md#stdlib-properties-kt-missinginheritedpropertyexception) with a message naming the property and the box), and
[`InheritanceFromContext`](workspace.md#stdlib-properties-kt-inheritancefromcontext) (same walk, but prefers each box's live Kotlin variables over raw
properties).

The rest is small conveniences: graph access (`named`, `+=` / `-=` for
connect/disconnect, `__m` markers); execution control (`begin`, `end`, `start`, `animate`,
`aside`, `cell`); frame-presentation logging (`frameLogStart`, `frameLogStop`,
`frameLogMark`, `frameLogLine`); matrix and buffer building (`mat4`, `mat3`, `FloatBuffer.add`,
`IntBuffer.add`, `ByteBuffer.putf16`); and terse numeric/collection/string shorthands
(`Number.f` / `.i` / `.l` / `.d`, `fa`, `ia`, `Int.alphas`, `String.times`, `List.m` / `.s`,
`String.r`, and `highlightSyntax` behind `String.h` / `String.ss`).

## playlist.kt { #playlist-kt }

Playlist functionality for Field4

This module provides helpers for executing boxes in a defined order based on their `playlist` property.
Boxes with a `playlist` property (a Double) will be executed in order from lowest to highest value.
Between each `begin()` call, `executePlaylist` waits `pauseList` `frame()` calls (default 1).

User-facing dev doc: dev_docs/Playlist.md (a pointer stub); this KDoc is the source of truth.

## stdlib_execution.kt { #stdlib-execution-kt }

The general-purpose helpers that every Field box already has in scope.

Box code is compiled with the standard imports in `intro` in its preamble and with `Box` as an
implicit receiver, so everything here — including the `Box.` extensions — can be called
unqualified from inside a box.

The substantial part is the property-delegate machinery that `prop` and `@exported` generate
against: [`Delegation`](workspace.md#stdlib-properties-kt-delegation) (stores on the receiver's own property bag), [`Inheritance`](workspace.md#stdlib-properties-kt-inheritance) (walks up
`parents` until some ancestor has the property, otherwise throws
[`MissingInheritedPropertyException`](workspace.md#stdlib-properties-kt-missinginheritedpropertyexception) with a message naming the property and the box), and
[`InheritanceFromContext`](workspace.md#stdlib-properties-kt-inheritancefromcontext) (same walk, but prefers each box's live Kotlin variables over raw
properties).

The rest is small conveniences: graph access (`named`, `+=` / `-=` for
connect/disconnect, `__m` markers); execution control (`begin`, `end`, `start`, `animate`,
`aside`, `cell`); frame-presentation logging (`frameLogStart`, `frameLogStop`,
`frameLogMark`, `frameLogLine`); matrix and buffer building (`mat4`, `mat3`, `FloatBuffer.add`,
`IntBuffer.add`, `ByteBuffer.putf16`); and terse numeric/collection/string shorthands
(`Number.f` / `.i` / `.l` / `.d`, `fa`, `ia`, `Int.alphas`, `String.times`, `List.m` / `.s`,
`String.r`, and `highlightSyntax` behind `String.h` / `String.ss`).

### LedgerSlot { #lifecycleledger-kt-ledgerslot }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">LedgerSlot</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">owner</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Any</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">key</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Any</span><span class="o">?</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/runtime/lifecycle/LifecycleLedger/#L167)

A coroutine scope with a manually stepped dispatcher. It creates no thread and registers no new box launcher. Use `withSimulationClock` inside ordinary `frames`; standard `launch` children inherit the box, source and parent job. `delay` and `withTimeout` then use simulation time. `advance` and `close` belong to the creating thread; dispatch and cancellation may enqueue from another thread.

A reusable build stage. `inputKeys` selects only the authored inputs this stage consumes, and may name [`StudyBuildGate`](workspace.md#studybuilds-kt-studybuildgate)s; `dependencies` names other stages whose current results must exist first, either in this runner or, written `dependsOn(runner, stage)`, in another runner of the same document. `recipeVersion` must change when the adapter or its relevant runtime changes. The runner does not infer code identity from a closure. `inputHelp` explains missing inputs without making the stage runnable or changing its fingerprint; a closed gate supplies its own explanation. `resultNotes` is a fast, pure presentation of a completed record's retained facts; it must not inspect mutable design state or change acceptance. It is shared by UI and agent tools and does not change build identity. Qualification gates belong in the build and input contracts. `build` runs on a worker and must use its captured context, not mutable live input.

The program is stopped, with every process it started, when the build is cancelled, when `deadline` passes, or when `stall` passes with no change to the progress file (or, without one, no new output). What a study can say about a picture in numbers, and how it lays pictures out for a model to look at. Every study that draws — StackSL, RectSL, a stack.auto slot — measures and lays out its frames here, so a measurement means the same thing in all of them.

### StudyVerb { #livestudy-kt-studyverb }

## QualifiedSource.kt { #qualifiedsource-kt }

### Qualified sources: changing a rule without breaking what already works

A rule (a placement recipe, a fallback, a solver strategy) is a source that other builds consume.
A [`QualifiedSource`](workspace.md#qualifiedsource-kt-qualifiedsource) keeps three things beside it and lets the rule change only when all three agree:

- the **rule**, a [`SourceStudy`](workspace.md#sourcestudy-kt-sourcestudy) over a box property;
- the **fixtures**, a [`SourceStudy`](workspace.md#sourcestudy-kt-sourcestudy) of retained real cases, each an exact input and the outcome the rule
  gave it ([`QualifiedFixture`](workspace.md#qualifiedsource-kt-qualifiedfixture));
- a **replay** stage, a [`StudyBuilds`](workspace.md#studybuilds-kt-studybuilds) runner that runs a candidate rule on every fixture and on a
  [`QualifiedControl`](workspace.md#qualifiedsource-kt-qualifiedcontrol), an input no correct rule can pass, which must fail.

A change starts as a *candidate*: a frozen record of the base it was made against, its source, the
fixtures, the dependencies and the checks ([`QualifiedCandidate`](workspace.md#qualifiedsource-kt-qualifiedcandidate)), named by the hash of all of them. The
replay compares each fixture's new outcome with the recorded one: the same, changed, or held (the rule
or its checks refused it). A candidate is admitted, and `apply` publishes it through
`SourceStudy.edit`, only when its replay is current, covers every fixture with the same outcome, the
control failed as it must, and nothing it depends on has changed.

The checks that judge a candidate are out of its reach ([`FrozenRegion`](workspace.md#qualifiedsource-kt-frozenregion)): files it may not edit, text
after a marker that must stay byte for byte, or a separate frozen copy. Only a person changes them, and
only a person changes a fixture's recorded outcome: `proposeRebaseline` draws each changed outcome with
an **Approve** button, and the press records who approved it and when. No tool approves.

`Box.qualifiedSource` makes one in a box and registers the agent tools `<name>.inspect`, `.candidate`,
`.test`, `.apply`, `.retainFixture` and `.proposeRebaseline`.

### QualifiedFixture { #qualifiedsource-kt-qualifiedfixture }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">QualifiedFixture</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">input</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">outcome</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Any</span><span class="o">?</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/study/source/QualifiedSource/#L127)

A retained case: the exact `input` text and the `outcome` the rule gave it, which must survive a JSON round trip.

### QualifiedControl { #qualifiedsource-kt-qualifiedcontrol }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">QualifiedControl</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">name</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">input</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">messageContains</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="o">?</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="kc">null</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/study/source/QualifiedSource/#L134)

An input no correct rule can pass, replayed with every candidate. Its replay must fail (the rule or its checks throw), with `messageContains` in the message when given. A control that passes means the checks are not running, so no candidate is admitted.

### FrozenRegion { #qualifiedsource-kt-frozenregion }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">sealed</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nc">FrozenRegion</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/study/source/QualifiedSource/#L143)

Where a qualified source keeps its checks out of a candidate's reach. A candidate breaking any of its regions is refused before it is saved. What the regions freeze is recorded in the candidate as `QualifiedCandidate.checks` and handed to the replay as `QualifiedReplay.checks`.

## SourceStudy.kt { #sourcestudy-kt }

The language-neutral half of a live-code study: the part of "talking a function into existence"
that does not care what the language is.

A study holds one editable source — the text in a box that a person and a model are both working
on — and a durable, append-only history of the versions of it that passed a check. Every change
arrives as a *transaction*: the caller names the revision it read and a hash of the live source it
read, the candidate is checked by the language adapter, and only then is it written into the box,
with a compare-and-swap against the text that is there *now*. So a model preparing an edit while a
person types cannot overwrite the person, a candidate that fails its check changes nothing, and
every accepted version can be read back, compared and restored.

What the language adds is one function, [`SourceStudy`](workspace.md#sourcestudy-kt-sourcestudy)'s `admit`: compile and check a candidate,
returning a value (whatever the language's tools need — a composition, a compiled shader report)
or throwing [`StudyRejection`](workspace.md#sourcestudy-kt-studyrejection) with a message a person or a model can act on. The StackSL, RectSL,
stack.auto and function studies are all adapters over it; `FunctionStudy` predated it and kept a
private copy of the protocol until 2026-09-29, with the same file layout, so a revision directory
written before then still reads.

### On disk

`directory/<id>.<extension>` is a revision's source and `directory/<id>.json` its metadata (parent,
description, time, and whatever facts the adapter chose to keep). `directory/HEAD` names the checked
revision the box last held. An id is `r<n>-<first 12 hex of SHA-256(source)>`, so an id also
verifies its own file: a revision whose source was edited on disk refuses to load.

This is trusted local code, not a sandbox: `admit` runs whatever the adapter runs. Cancellation
(`cancel`) stops a pending publication, not a computation that never checks for it.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/study/source/SourceStudy.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/study/source/SourceStudy/)

**Used in:** [Studies](../studies.md)

## stdlib_output.kt { #stdlib-output-kt }

The general-purpose helpers that every Field box already has in scope.

Box code is compiled with the standard imports in `intro` in its preamble and with `Box` as an
implicit receiver, so everything here — including the `Box.` extensions — can be called
unqualified from inside a box.

The substantial part is the property-delegate machinery that `prop` and `@exported` generate
against: [`Delegation`](workspace.md#stdlib-properties-kt-delegation) (stores on the receiver's own property bag), [`Inheritance`](workspace.md#stdlib-properties-kt-inheritance) (walks up
`parents` until some ancestor has the property, otherwise throws
[`MissingInheritedPropertyException`](workspace.md#stdlib-properties-kt-missinginheritedpropertyexception) with a message naming the property and the box), and
[`InheritanceFromContext`](workspace.md#stdlib-properties-kt-inheritancefromcontext) (same walk, but prefers each box's live Kotlin variables over raw
properties).

The rest is small conveniences: graph access (`named`, `+=` / `-=` for
connect/disconnect, `__m` markers); execution control (`begin`, `end`, `start`, `animate`,
`aside`, `cell`); frame-presentation logging (`frameLogStart`, `frameLogStop`,
`frameLogMark`, `frameLogLine`); matrix and buffer building (`mat4`, `mat3`, `FloatBuffer.add`,
`IntBuffer.add`, `ByteBuffer.putf16`); and terse numeric/collection/string shorthands
(`Number.f` / `.i` / `.l` / `.d`, `fa`, `ia`, `Int.alphas`, `String.times`, `List.m` / `.s`,
`String.r`, and `highlightSyntax` behind `String.h` / `String.ss`).
